evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0h = 11.80 mg/L, min observed ~9.2 mg/L (27.8h), constraint 2.0 mg/L
Receiving P(48h) = 2.47 g/L vs sources 2.98-3.06 g/L; slope 0.88 g/L @36h to 2.47 g/L @48h matches source-like growth
No sustained DO2 decline or divergence from source profiles in 0-52h receiving observations
args.rationale: Receiving run is healthy at decision time 52h: DO2 ~11.8 mg/L (historical min ~9.2, far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum), no oxygen-constraint risk, and product concentration (2.47 g/L at 48h) is rising on a trajectory comparable to source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L at 48h). Feed reduction would sacrifice product mass without evidence of overload; increased aeration addresses no deficit; stop yields zero production. Normal case — no intervention.
args.uncertainty: Receiving P is ~15-20% below source values at matched assay times, which could indicate a mildly suboptimal (e.g., scale-transfer) effect; however, with no DO2 stress signal and rising product, the risk of any intervention reducing counted product mass outweighs speculative gains. Hidden receiving parameters make quantitative benefit of interventions unverifiable.
